mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has risen monotonically across the four observed weeks (-17.7 to -10.9), showing that commuting routines are being restored. Restored commuting adds weekday lunch, errand and after-work trips that land in retail venues, so RETAIL_REC continues its recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose in each of the last four weekly means
failure_condition: WORKPLACES keeps rising for two more weekly prints while the mean of RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days is equal to or below the mean of RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen in every observed week (14.0 to 11.7), meaning households are steadily replacing home time with out-of-home time. That substitution directly frees shopping and leisure trips, so RETAIL_REC is higher over the next four weeks than over the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined by 2.3 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to decline for two more weekly prints while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A RESIDENTIAL print below 12.0 marks the crossing of a behavioural threshold where enough households have re-established out-of-home routines that retail footfall accelerates. The threshold therefore predicts a faster RETAIL_REC gain within two weeks than the linear trend alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL prints below 12.0 in any week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is 11.7, already below 12.0
failure_condition: Within two weeks of RESIDENTIAL printing below 12.0, the two-week mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its mean over the two weeks preceding the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has recovered 6.2 points over four weeks (-30.9 to -24.7) and is the highest-frequency indicator of discretionary trip-making. When TRANSIT crosses above -24.0, discretionary trip volume is high enough that retail venues capture a disproportionate share, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT prints above -24.0 (gap to baseline narrower than 24 points)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -30.9 to -24.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: After TRANSIT prints above -24.0, the mean of RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is not higher than the mean over the 14 days before the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery is jointly gated by commuting and discretionary transit: only when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise in the same week is the full trip bundle (commute plus non-work errand) restored. Joint weekly gains therefore produce larger RETAIL_REC increases than either series alone, and any single-series stall caps the retail gain.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week in the same week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rose in each of the last two weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks where both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together, the following 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is no higher than in weeks where only one of them rises.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM at -4.3 remains much closer to baseline than RETAIL_REC at -20.3, showing that essential shopping has normalised while discretionary shopping has not. As the gap GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC narrows, essential-only trip behaviour relaxes and grocery trips convert into retail-and-recreation trips within one week.
candidate_trigger: the gap GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC narrows by more than 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is 16.0 points above RETAIL_REC at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where the GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC gap narrows by more than 1 point, the next week's RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the current week's RETAIL_REC mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active policy-easing regime, capacity and hour limits on retail venues are relaxed, so the mobility recovery already visible in TRANSIT passes into measured retail activity with roughly a four-week transmission lag. The easing regime is what makes the transit-to-retail pass-through positive rather than offset by venue caps.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recovered toward baseline over the last four weeks
regime_hint: policy easing with retail capacity limits being relaxed
failure_condition: In a confirmed policy-easing regime, the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the last-28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue to recover.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS is the most weather-sensitive series and swung between -9.3 and -12.6 across the window. Weeks in which PARKS drops sharply indicate outdoor-suppressing weather, which shifts leisure spending indoors into retail-and-recreation venues and produces a one-week RETAIL_REC uplift.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 3.3 points from t-2w to t-1w while RETAIL_REC rose 1.5 points
regime_hint: seasonal weather volatility with outdoor-suppressing weeks
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS falls by more than 3 points week-on-week, the following week's RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the week of the PARKS drop.
